title: telemetry-experimenter: tenant defaults dry-run & quant-tier mapper
author: Jordan Kim
description:
Motivation: teams need safer, tenant-specific defaults for batching, KV cache retention, and quantization tier selection but configuring these heuristics manually is error-prone and slow. This PR introduces a telemetry-driven "experimenter" service that generates candidate tenant defaults, runs a dry-run simulator on historical traces, and emits an explainable unit-econ score for each candidate. The goal is to provide safe, actionable suggestions (exportable YAML) and a CLI for ops to validate changes before promoting them to tenant defaults.

What this PR does (high level):
- New microservice: services/telemetry-experimenter - consumes summarized telemetry (latency/cost/token-distributions/cache-hit-profiles) and materializes candidate configurations for batching, cache TTLs, and quantization tiers.
- Dry-run simulator CLI: cli/rw-defaults-dryrun - replays sampled historical traces against candidate configs to compute expected P95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, and delta in cost-per-1M-tokens.
- Unit-econ scorer: pkg/econ/tenant_score.go - multiplies normalized latency, cost, failure-rate and quality-regression signals into a single score and per-dimension breakdown used by console suggestions UI.
- Safe promotion API: console/api/suggestions.go (stubbed) and services/telemetry-experimenter/promote_guard.go implement conservative guardrails (cold-start safety, max-cost-multipliers, fallback to parent defaults).
- Storage/migration: infra/migrations/20260201_create_experiment_runs.sql to persist experiment runs and confidence intervals.
- Docs: docs/telemetry-experimenter.md and runbook for oncall.

Checklist: 
- [x] ingestion + sampling from telemetry stream
- [x] candidate generator for batch/cache/quant space
- [x] dry-run simulator + CLI
- [x] unit-econ scoring and explainability fields
- [x] DB migration and simple retention policy for experiment runs
- [x] integration tests & lightweight benchmark harness
- [x] docs and runbook

Behavioral guarantees & safety:
- All suggestions are opt-in; the default is no automatic promotion.
- Dry-run must be executed prior to any automatic promotion in canary channel.
- Promotion has a configurable max-cost-multiplier and rollback timeout.

Testing: includes a small integration fixture with sampled traces (tests/integration/experimenter_fixtures.yaml) and a new CI job (ci/experimenter-integration) that replays fixtures and asserts unit-econ improvement >= -1% (no regression allowed without manual approval).

Notes on scope: the console integration is intentionally minimal (suggestions endpoint + export); a later PR will add UI surfaces for A/B rollout controls. This PR focuses on the core telemetry -> candidate -> dry-run -> score pipeline.

review_comments: Aisha Malik: Overall this is great. Two asks: add a retention claim for experiment_runs (so we don't accumulate heavy state) and prove the dry-run matches real runtimes for at least one tenant.
Author (Jordan Kim): Added a retention TTL in the migration and included a small cross-tenant replica in the fixtures. Added a note in docs about sample size expectations.
Diego Fernandez: Can you add unit tests for the econ scorer edge cases (e.g., when latency improves but quality drops)?

Author (Jordan Kim): Added econ scorer unit tests and an explainability output that returns per-dimension scores to the CLI. CI test added (experimenter-integration) verifies no quality regressions beyond threshold.
Ruth Chen: Concerned about PII in telemetry. Are we sampling/aggregating before ingestion?
Author (Jordan Kim): Yes — summarizer emits only aggregated histogram buckets and token-length aggregates. Added a privacy note in docs and a small sanitization step in pkg/telemetry/summarizer.go.
release_notes: Adds a telemetry-driven 'experimenter' service that can propose tenant-specific batching/cache/quant defaults and a dry-run CLI to validate their impact. Includes DB migration, unit-econ scoring, and a conservative promotion guard. Opt-in only; no automatic promotions enabled by default.
summary: Introduce a telemetry-based experimenter that generates and dry-runs tenant defaults (batch/cache/quant) and scores candidates for safe promotion.
risk_profile: low-medium: core runtime unchanged; new service and DB table added. Promotion and automatic rollouts are gated and opt-in. Integration tests included.
notes_for_release_engineering: Run infra/migrations/20260201_create_experiment_runs.sql before deploying services/telemetry-experimenter. Ensure the summarizer stream is configured in staging and CI job ci/experimenter-integration is enabled for the canary channel.
